title: 2026-05-19-crew-collage-and-decision-council
summary: Leadership reviewed Q2 metrics, flagged a two-week capacity provisioning decision, and prioritized reliability work for the serving runtime. People update included a targeted hiring pause for non-customer-facing ICs; security confirmed SOC2 roadmap on schedule. Action items focus on a short pilot for a new autoscaling policy, an updated runbook for Private installs, and an investment decision for burst capacity by 2026-06-02.
action_items: Maya Patel - Publish updated product roadmap doc and call out reliability milestones - 2026-05-26
Carlos Mendes - Run end-to-end latency stress test and share results + raw traces - 2026-05-28
Liam O'Connor - Draft capacity vs. cost proposal for burst vs. reserved and send to execs - 2026-06-02
Joanne Kim - Confirm hiring exceptions and update internal FAQ - 2026-05-21
Security Team (Nadia) - Post SOC2 interim status and KMS integration notes - 2026-05-25
next_steps: Execs to decide on burst capacity purchase by 2026-06-02
Small pilot of the new autoscaler starts 2026-05-24 (Ops+Infra)
Company-wide AMA scheduled for 2026-05-26 to walk changes
Follow-up doc: runbook for Private installs to be linked in #infra
transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-05-19 10:00 PDT; Duration: ~71 minutes; Host: Priya Anand; Location: Zoom (recorded).

[00:00] Priya Anand: Okay, hey everybody, thanks for hopping on. Uh, quick housekeeping — this is recorded, captions are on, and we have the agenda up in the chat. We're going to keep it to 60-ish minutes and then open to Q&A.
[00:18] Priya Anand: Quick wins first — product and reliability updates, then people, then business, then decisions. Liam, can you kick off with the infra summary?
[00:30] Liam O'Connor: Yeah sure, thanks. Good morning. So, short story — latency improved a hair, median down 6% across the hosted fleet after the compilation changes we shipped last week. We still see tail spikes on long contexts though, so the KV cache behavior is a target, um K V cash, as the transcriber might write it, sorry.
[00:50] Liam O'Connor: The runtime team identified two hotspots: attention kernel in high-token streams, and gc pauses when the KV cache evicts lots of segments. We've got a patch queued that reduces lock contention, but it needs a canary and an A/B run. Carlos will walk through the rollout plan.
[01:10] Carlos Mendes: Hey all — plan is a three-stage canary: internal-only, then dedicated pools, then hosted. We'll cap traffic on the canary to limit blast radius. Expect the canary to run 72 hours, then we evaluate. If all good, full rollout the following week.
[01:28] Carlos Mendes: Also, we're proposing a temporary burst capacity buy to cover predicted bot traffic for Product X. Liam and I will put numbers in a short doc for exec review.
[01:36] Priya Anand: Can you pin a decision date? We need to be clear for finance.
[01:40] Carlos Mendes: Yes — target decision: 2026-06-02.
[01:44] Priya Anand: Great.
[01:47] Maya Patel: I'll highlight that on the roadmap when I share the update later — the reliability milestones bump our delivery timelines for a couple items but protect customer SLAs.
[02:01] Priya Anand: Cool — Sales, Ethan, quick update on pipeline and churn.
[02:06] Ethan Zhao: Thanks. Quarter-to-date net-new ARR is flat vs plan, but we have two inbound proof-of-concepts that could convert in Q3 if they like our performance numbers. Renewals look solid; churn is low. Biggest ask from customers is more deterministic latency and better private deployment docs — customers trying Private want clear install runbooks and audit logs.
[02:28] Ethan Zhao: Also, pricing questions on Dedicated vs hosted — teams are weighing predictable reserved capacity vs pay-as-you-go. We'll try to push clearer guidance on the site.
[02:40] Priya Anand: Thanks. Joanne, people update?
[02:44] Joanne Kim: Quick one — headcount: we reached 149 full time as of last week. Given the runway and the exec ask to tighten non-customer-facing hires, we're instituting a temporary slow-down for non-critical IC hiring effective immediately. Hiring for customer-facing roles and critical infra safety work continues. Exceptions by manager request to me. We'll publish an FAQ.
[03:04] Joanne Kim: Also we've got a small reskilling stipend for folks moving from project-based roles into critical infra reliability projects. Details in HR drop this afternoon.
[03:12] Priya Anand: Appreciate that. A couple of security notes — Nadia?
[03:17] Nadia Ortiz: Hi — SOC2 progress is on track for the Type II window. Pen test findings: two mediums were closed, one is in remediation and should be closed by next week. KMS integration for Private customers: we've completed the API surface and a first customer test is green, but we need to document the exact key rotation expectations. We'll post the interim doc to Confluence and link from the Private readme.
[03:40] Priya Anand: Any compliance blockers for sales?
[03:43] Ethan Zhao: Not blockers, but customers asked for clearer retention and audit log examples — they're often asking to see sample entries. If we can provide that, it unblocks several pilots.
[03:52] Nadia Ortiz: We'll export a sanitized example and share in a repo.
[03:56] Priya Anand: Thank you.
[04:00] [04:00] Audience: (applause emote in chat)
[04:10] Priya Anand: Ok now some business numbers — high level. Revenue pace is trending inline but margin pressure from GPU spot prices is real. Our cost per token has ticked up slightly; Optimize recommendations have shaved some of that but we need the autoscaler pilot to see additional gains.
[04:31] Priya Anand: We're also seeing model-side spending where bigger seq lengths blow up unit cost. Product and research — any quick notes? Samir?
[04:39] Samir Nair: Research is shipping two model variants optimized for short-turn interactions and long-context ones. That lets the smart routing pick variants to reduce cost for customers. Early internal evals show up to 22% CPU reduction on some workloads. We'll publish a benchmark sheet.
[04:59] Maya Patel: That's the routing piece that ties into Optimize — we'll bake that into the recommendations. Next week I'll push a doc that ties specific customer patterns to recommended model/quantization choices.
[05:12] Priya Anand: Okay — decision items. We need a clear tradeoff for burst capacity: spend now on burst vs push customers to dedicated. Liam, can you add the risk table?
[05:23] Liam O'Connor: Yep, we'll put failure modes, RTOs, and cost delta.
[05:27] [05:27] Q&A opens.
[05:28] Audience (Speaker 1): Hi, question for infra — during the canary, what telemetry will we collect?
[05:33] Carlos Mendes: We'll collect p99/p999 latencies, kernel-level counters, and KV eviction rates. Also full trace capture for 1% of requests so we can pull individual traces.
[05:44] Audience (Speaker 2): On Private installs — how do we handle KMS if a customer is air-gapped?
[05:49] Nadia Ortiz: For air-gapped installs, the current pattern is HSM support on-prem and a proxy key rotation tool we'll ship in the next release. It's more manual but we've validated with a partner. We'll add steps to the runbook.
[06:05] Audience (Speaker 3): Any hiring bullets for infra?
[06:08] Joanne Kim: We're prioritizing two SRE ICs for the runtime team — approval is in flight.
[06:12] Priya Anand: Quick callout — internal credit: the runtime team's done a lot of heavy lifting. Please take a minute to thank them in the #shoutouts channel.
[06:21] [06:21] (short silence, some laughter)
[06:28] Priya Anand: Alright — a few operational clarifications. We're moving the weekly leadership sync to Fridays starting next week to align with release cycles. Also, the new incident postmortem template (Carlos) is mandatory for sev2+ incidents.
[06:43] Carlos Mendes: I'll post the template and a short walkthrough doc.
[06:47] Priya Anand: On the customer front — we will trial a mid-quarter executive briefing for our largest customers to improve retention; Ethan, coordinate with Customer Success, please.
[06:57] Ethan Zhao: On it.
[07:00] Priya Anand: Okay final — people Qs.
[07:02] Audience (Speaker 4): Will there be salary freezes?
[07:06] Joanne Kim: No company-wide salary freeze. We'll tighten hiring, but compensation philosophy remains. Any exceptions will be communicated by managers.
[07:16] Audience (Speaker 5): Are there plans to open another office in EMEA?
[07:19] Priya Anand: Not immediate. We are exploring regionally-focused partners and potentially an EMEA lead role later this year.
[07:28] Priya Anand: Closing remarks — big thanks for the heavy lifting on the runtime patches. We made tradeoffs to protect customers that will slow some new feature delivery, but that's the right call. We'll reconvene on the burst decision 2026-06-02.
[07:44] Priya Anand: Okay that's it. We'll post slides and the recording. See you at the AMA on Tuesday.
[07:52] (meeting ends)

Notes: Transcript includes occasional mis-attributions and filler words; technical terms sometimes flattened (e.g., KV cache -> K V cash). References to docs and links were shared in the chat ("runbook link", "burst-capacity-proposal.docx").
